description: The Road Network Files (RNF) from Statistics Canada are digital representations of Canada's national road network containing street names, types, directions and address ranges. Statistics Canada lists user applications such as mapping, geocoding, geographic searching, area delineation and database maintenance. Files exist for census years (2001, 2006, 2011, 2016 and 2021) and for intercensal years from 2005 to 2025. The 2016 Census RNF also gives the unique identifier, name and type of each side of a street arc for provinces and territories, census subdivisions, census metropolitan areas and census agglomerations, and ranks streets in five levels of detail for small to medium scale mapping. Coverage is national. The files are available to download as shapefile and GML (English and French editions, with a reference guide), free under the Open Government Licence - Canada, and are also listed on the Open Government Portal and copied in university repositories. Caveats: Statistics Canada stresses that relative positional accuracy takes precedence over absolute accuracy, so the files are not suitable for engineering, emergency dispatching, surveying or legal applications, and they carry no traffic or physical road attributes. Because they link streets to census geography they support demand and exposure models that join population to the road network, for example for evacuation or accessibility studies. They complement the National Road Network (NRN), which carries lanes, surface and structures.
